title: Rav Zutra bar Tuviah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav’s student, and Hyman cites the following passages for his reports in Rav’s name: [Berakhot 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.7a.3) and [43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43b.3-5), [Shabbat 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.75a.2-3), [Pesachim 87a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.87a.9-10), [Yoma 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.39b.8), [Taanit 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.16b.2), [Chagigah 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12a.13) and [13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.13b.14), [Nedarim 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.41b.4), [Bava Metzia 59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.59a.3), [Bava Batra 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.97a.12), [Sanhedrin 106a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.106a.16), [Avodah Zarah 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.24b.14), [Makkot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.6b.3) and [12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.12a.10), [Zevachim 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.64b.10) and [Menachot 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.11a.8). Afterward he sat before Rav Yehudah, as in [Moed Katan 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16b.14-15), where he was reciting the Scripture lesson before Rav Yehudah; Zutra asked Rav Yehudah, who did not answer; Zutra asked a second time. Rav Yehudah said: “Because he does not know the explanation of this verse, is he not a great man?” He realized that he had taken the matter to heart (that Rav Yehudah was angry with him), and Rav Zutra bar Tuviah observed a period of admonition for himself for one day. Rav Zutra bar Tuviah also speaks in Rav Nachman’s name in [Yoma 86b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.86b.9).

His halakhot we find in [Yevamot 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.44a.7), where he said that he does not perform chalitzah for both, for the verse says “the house of the one whose shoe was removed”; in [Gittin 86b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.86b.8) he raises an objection to Rav’s words; and in [Menachot 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.11a.19-20) he challenges Rabbi Elazar’s words. Hyman notes that for the most part it is written “Rav Zutra bar Tuviah” with a heh, which Hyman takes to distinguish him from the later Rav Zutra bar Tuvia, which is with an aleph.[^3]

notes.text: פסק סידרא means reciting a Scripture lesson, not dividing verses. Saved Davidson Moed Katan16b shows Zutra asking and Yehudah declining to answer, then Zutra observing a one-day nezifah, an admonition rather than formal excommunication. Hyman’s heh/aleph spelling distinction remains his claim, without global identity binding.

Moed Katan 16b directly has Zutra reciting Scripture, asking Yehudah twice and observing a one-day nezifah after the rebuke. This is an admonition rather than formal excommunication. Hyman’s heh-versus-aleph name-spelling distinction remains his argument, not a global identity rule.

[Seder HaDorot 1089](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1089&lang=en) discusses the group of three teachings in Rav’s name at [Shabbat 75a:2–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.75a.2-3) alongside other transmissions from Rav. In [Yoma 39b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.39b.8), Zutra gives the statement without naming Rav. The linked [Chagigah 12a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12a.13) and [Makkot 6b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.6b.3) already spell Tuvia with an aleph, even though the teaching there is given in Rav’s name.
